recipes.name: Baked Coconut Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly coat a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Rinse shrimp; pat dry with paper towels.
Combine cornstarch, salt, and cayenne pepper in a shallow bowl. Add coconut flakes to a separate shallow bowl. Beat egg whites in a third shallow bowl until foamy.

Dredge 1 shrimp in cornstarch mixture; shake off excess. Dip into beaten egg whites. Left up so excess drips back into the bowl. Press into coconut to completely coat. Place coated shrimp, unstacked, on the prepared baking sheet. Repeat with remaining shrimp.
Bake in the preheated oven until outsides bright pink, centers opaque and no longer transparent, and coconut is browned, 15 to 20 minutes, flipping shrimp halfway through.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Coconut Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: This baked coconut shrimp recipe comes out perfectly crisp and golden after just 15 minutes in a hot oven. You'll wonder why you ever deep fried them.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delicious! Here's the orange marmalade sauce recipe I used: 1 cup of orange marmalade, two tablespoons horseradish, and two tablespoons dijon mustard.

We love coconut shrimp so I was very happy to see this recipe chosen for the Recipe Group this week. We prepared these exactly as written and they are absolutely perfect. They took 14 minutes on convection bake in my oven. The shrimp were perfectly cooked and the coconut breading was crunchy and very flavorful, but not overly sweet. I found a copy-cat recipe on-line for Outback's sauce that they serve with these - 1/2 cup orange marmalade, 2 teaspoons stone ground mustard with seeds, 1 teaspoon prepared horseradish and a dash of salt. It really does taste exactly like Outback's. We will be making and enjoying these often. Thanks for sharing!

I made half the recipe for dinner tonight and the shrimp were wonderful. I used the convection feature on my oven and baked the shrimp at 375 F. for about 15 min. Some of my shrimp were larger than the others, but they all came out perfectly cooked and not tough or rubbery. I used salt, pepper and garlic pdr. and dipped shrimp in a whole beaten egg. I also had to make my own sweetened coconut with a half bag of unsweetened coconut and 1 T powdered sugar. My coconut was old and a bit dry, so I added a scant teaspoon of water and microwaved it for 10-12 seconds and it was perfectly soft and fluffy and sweetened. I'll save that recipe for when I use the other half of the dry coconut. Thanks for the shrimp recipe, I'll be using it again soon.

I have been making several coconut shrimp recipes lately, both fried and baked. This one is the best. In order to get that evenly browned look and crunchy taste, I tweaked the coconut. First I pulsed it until quite fine in a small food processor, and then I LIGHTLY toasted it a large frying pan in 2 batches. Then made as directed, gently pressing the coconut to the shrimp on both sides and the ends. It adhered well. When it baked. it browned a little more and gave me the appearance and crunch I was seeking... perfect. I sprayed the pan with Pam, and for large shrimp, I baked 7 minutes on each side and lightly sprayed Pam on the top just before turning. To cut even more calories and reduce sugar, I used 1/2 cup Polaner's Sugar free Orange Marmalade, 2 tea horseradish , 2 tea stone ground dijon mustard, 1 pkg of Equal, and a pinch of salt for the marmalade. This is a much healthier version of one of my favorite foods. Worthy of special company, but I'll be making it often for the family.

It is very good, and popular with people. I used my food processor to make the coconut much finer, and only used about an eigth tsp. of cayenne, because older people can't handle the spice! Most of us, anyway! This is the second time I've made it, and I have learned the best way to proceed. the minute the coconut gets wet from dipping several wet shrimp in it, it no longer sticks. It's a royal pain. So I put just a little of the coconut in a small ramekin, did a couple of shrimp, then wiped it out, and added a little more, and put a little on top of the shrimp with my fingers. Then it went much faster and prevented all my hair from falling out from frustration!

Excellent! We loved the coconut shrimp, years ago, at the famous Lorelei restaurant in Islamorada, Florida. These were nearly as good, even though they are baked instead of deep fried. I followed the recipe closely, with the following deviations: I lined the baking sheet with parchment instead of using cooking spray. I know from experience that I would have more cornstarch on my fingers than on the shrimp if I dredged and dipped them one at a time into all 3 bowls, so I dredged all of the shrimp in the corn starch at the same time, then dipped them one at a time into the egg whites and coconut. I needed a little more coconut than called for, maybe 2 extra tablespoons. They were beautifully toasted and perfectly cooked in 15 minutes in my convection oven, which was preheated to 400 F, but then turned down to 350 F at the halfway point, while turning the shrimp. I regret that I didn’t have any dipping sauce ready. Next time I will definitely serve with some dipping sauces.

Incredible! I was skeptical of it being as good as the ratings say because if I’m honest, I can screw up a recipe real quick! But this was so so good! The only thing I did different was turned on the broiler for a minute or two at the end to crisp up the coconut a bit more.
I also made the dipping sauce suggested by others which was stellar! (1 cup Orange marmalade, 2 tsp stone ground mustard, 2 tsp horseradish)

Tasted good, made the orange marmalade dip with spicy mustard and cayenne (had to use what I had). Two things I will do differently next time: 1- I will spray my baking surface a little more to prevent sticking. I finally used a plastic spatula to be able to flip halfway through cooking. Tongs didn’t work at all! 2-To save some time I will try shaking a group of shrimp in the cornstarch coating in a bag to save some time before dipping individually in the egg white and coconut. Would love to make this again but it was more time consuming than expected.

This was quick and easy! I added a little flour to the cornstarch and just dipped them in a whole egg beaten then the coconut...fantastic! All the crunch and no oil! I also made a dipping sauce of Coco Loco drink mix, pineapple ice cream topping and Dijon mustard...my husband absolutely loved it!
A recipe I will always use for crusted shrimp, very good flavor! I added panko crumbs as well for extra crunch!! Just needing to find a good sauce to dip them in. Other than that perfect dish
Recipe is pretty good, I will make again! The only adjustments I made were I added about double the cyan and put my coconut in a food processor to make it more fine, turned out great.

I've made several times.... I lightly sprayed shrimp with cooking spray, after placing on baking sheet and after turning them over. This helps to brown the coconut. I agree with several comments, NO sauce is needed. I am drooling already and want to make these asap.
Spectacular! The flavor, crunch, and texture are spot on. You will not miss the grease. All you experience is sweet shrimp and sweet coconut. Easy peasy.

I made this tonight for my husband and I. It is messy to put together, but it was very tasty! We both tried to dip the shrimp into different sauces, but none was needed. Served with mashed sweet potatoes. Will make again!

I made this but didn't want to use egg white, without the yolk so I used Chia seed eggs, which are easy to make but you need to add more water than they ask for in the recipe. (1 Tbsp of chia seeds and 3 Tbsp of hot water, let sit and it gets gooey... add water so it's got an egg consistency AND I like to grind this up so it's not just chia seeds but more of a paste..... add that water.) Anyway, I made this added Tropical Traditions Coconut cream to the chia seed eggs but everything else was the same. I made that Outback recipe too (sort of). It was all delicious! Thanks so much!
Very easy, great taste. It took 10 minutes on each side with my oven. I was done with the whole process in about 40 minutes!
I’ve tried several recipes for coconut shrimp and this is by far the best!

I had enjoyed a coconut shrimp dish at a nice restaurant and was looking forward to make it at home. This recipe does not require frying and easily delivered that tasty experience and more. I love the taste of freshly made seafood at home. The orange marmalade as a dip pairs incredibly well with the dish. A crowd pleaser for sure.
I thought this was very dry. I won't make it again.
